analysis.title: The SMID Point
key_insights: Oceaneering (OII) fell more than 16% after earnings and has recovered most of the loss, now down about 5%. The main issue was 4Q EBITDA guidance of $85-95mm versus consensus of $105mm at the time.
OII initial 2027 EBITDA guidance is $430-480mm, with a $455mm midpoint modestly below expectations. Citi trims 2027 revenue by 1.5% to $3.12B (+6% y/y) and EBITDA by 2% to $458mm.

OII AdTech (+17%) is the primary growth driver, but Citi cuts segment margins to about 12% from about 14%. SSR is held at 6% y/y growth in 2027 off a more modest 2026, with segment revenues trimmed 2%.
Citi rates OII Neutral with a $45 target. At about 8.5x 2027E EBITDA it sees limited upside, despite exposure to both offshore oilfield growth and marine defense spending.

O-I Glass (OI) fell 12.4% after a 3Q miss and a cut to 2026 guidance. Volume weakness (-$45mm, including the US/Canada trade dispute) was larger than Citi expected, and diesel/freight headwinds were -$35mm versus the 2Q outlook.

OI lowered Fit to Win savings by $20-45mm for 2026 because of the pace of recovery in Europe. Citi forecasts negative EBIT in Europe in 4Q26 and a gradual recovery in 2027 as renewed contracts layer in through 1Q.

For 2027, OI points to $170mm+ of Fit to Win savings and stable volumes, partly offset by incentive comp resetting. Net price could improve as annual contracts renew amid high energy costs and tighter industry supply/demand. Over 90% of European energy costs are hedged for 2027 (100% in 1Q) below the current TTF forward curve. Citi rates OI Buy with an $8 target.
Polaris (PII) shares rose Tuesday but faded into the close. The 3Q raise is the third of the year, helped by retail growth against a difficult comparison, strong margins and good inventory.

Polaris management discussion centered on the puts and takes for 2027 margins, which add to an unpredictable demand environment. Citi says 2027/2028 earnings power is an open debate, but Polaris has raised its floor and valuation has largely reset. Rating Neutral, target $61.

Wingstop (WING) delivered sequentially improving same-store sales and appears to have set a low bar for 4Q: flattish with 3Q despite more time behind the ad strategy shifts and a significant bump in marketing spend. Citi rates it Buy with a $185 target.

Wingstop may have moved to a more realistic unit growth outlook that balances unit economics with current SSS trends. Citi expects the longer-term debate on the right SSS path and on competing for core QSR customers with premium positioning to continue, but sees the near-term sequential top-line path as favorable.

HHS issued an interim enforcement-discretion policy for 503A peptide compounding that preserves access to six wellness peptides while FDA completes formal rulemaking. None of the peptides is FDA-approved, and the policy does not establish safety or efficacy. Access comes with 10 conditions covering prescribing, sourcing, testing, formulation, labeling, dispensing and adverse-event reporting.

Citi's Geoff Meacham sees the narrow scope as a clearer boundary around products that do not qualify for discretion. He says this lays groundwork for stricter enforcement on compounds under FDA review, including Lilly's retatrutide (submission 1Q27), and on copies of FDA-approved products.
